executionHost.removeActiveBusy: {label} is the host this window is driving, and a turn is in flight on it. Removing it returns this window to this machine at once, and the running turn stays on the host.

overview.noStreams: No event stream is open right now.
overview.conflictTitle: This host and the local record disagree
overview.conflictBody: The host's answer is shown above and is the one enforced. The local mirror is stale — it was most likely changed from the CLI or the Owner API.

capabilities.neverReportedTitle: This device has never reported its capabilities
capabilities.neverReportedBody: Nothing below is confirmed. Entries marked Expected come from the platform baseline; the rest are simply unknown. The device reports on its next connection.

noVocabulary.local: This machine's capabilities are probed locally rather than reported.
noVocabulary.paired-device: This device has not reported, and its platform is unknown, so there is no baseline to infer from.
noVocabulary.remote-host: This host has not completed a capability exchange yet. Connect to it to read its manifest.
noVocabulary.worker: A worker is enrolled with SecurityStore capability ids, which are a different vocabulary from platform capabilities, so there is no platform matrix to show.
noVocabulary.ssh-host: An SSH server never reports anything and holds no capability set of ours. Nothing here is absent, it was simply never asked.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.browserLocalBody: These are this browser's local capabilities. Execution capabilities belong to the paired Host; select its row in the device list to inspect them. The browser capability means an agent-controlled browser engine, not this browser window.

ssh.title: SSH
ssh.shellOnly: A shell and nothing else. No agent, workspace or sandbox runs over SSH.
ssh.credentialRequiredBody: {name} uses password authentication and no password is stored. Add one in Settings → Terminal before connecting.
ssh.unknownHostBody: Nothing in Settings → Terminal matches {ref}. The profile was renamed or removed after this row was listed; reopen Settings to add it back.

auth.passwordSaved: A password is stored in this machine's keyring.
auth.passwordMissing: No password stored, so connecting will fail.
auth.passphraseSaved: A passphrase is stored in this machine's keyring.

ssh.chainBrokenBody: A host on the way to this one is missing, points back at itself, or the chain is longer than five hops. Connecting is refused rather than falling back to a direct connection, which would reach a different machine. Fix the jump host in Settings → Terminal.
ssh.forwardsLoopback: Both ends always bind 127.0.0.1. A forward reachable from the network would turn one machine into an open relay for the other.

probe.cost: A test opens a real connection. It authenticates through every jump host, appears in their logs, may ask an ssh-agent for a passphrase, and trusts the host key if this is the first time. It never opens a port forward.
probe.desktopOnly: Testing a connection dials from this machine, so it can only be done from the desktop app. Opening a shell still works here: the paired desktop dials for you.
probe.invalid: This profile cannot produce a connection ({reason}), so the host was never contacted. Fix it in Settings → Terminal.
probe.reachableLearned: Reachable. This was the first connection, so the host key has now been trusted and saved.
probe.reachableVerified: Reachable. The host key matched the one already trusted.

invalidReason.name: it has no display name
invalidReason.host: its host address is empty or contains spaces
invalidReason.username: its username is empty or contains spaces
invalidReason.privateKeyPath: private-key authentication has no key path
invalidReason.jumpChain: its jump host is missing, loops back, or is incomplete

ssh.viaHostBody: This shell does not hold SSH credentials, so the paired host opens the connection with the key or password it keeps. Only hosts the host's own desktop has registered can be opened this way, and no host key is reported back over this transport.
ssh.noHostTitle: No terminal host to connect through
ssh.noHostBody: SSH runs on a machine, not in a browser tab. Pair a host, or open the desktop app, and this host becomes connectable again.
ssh.credentialRequiredBastionBody: “{name}” connects through “{bastion}”, which uses a password and has none stored. Save one on “{bastion}” in the SSH hosts editor, then connect.

description.local: What this console asks of every machine, and why this one has no answer.
description.paired-device: What this console asks of every machine, and why a paired device has no answer.
description.remote-host: What this console asks of every machine, and why a remote host has no answer from here.
description.worker: What this console asks of every machine, and why a worker has no answer.
description.ssh-host: What this console asks of every machine, and why an SSH host has no answer.

title: Devices
description: Every machine this account can reach, what it can do, and what it is allowed to do here.
attentionCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 needs attention} other {# need attention}}
hostUnreachableBody: This host could not be asked, so lifecycle state and the exact capabilities behind each grant come from the local mirror. A device suspended elsewhere may still read as active.
missingLinkTitle: That device is not in this fleet
missingLinkBody: The link names a device that is no longer paired or added here, so this machine is shown instead.

actions.refreshFailed: Could not refresh the device list
actions.grow: Pair a device or add a host

detail.noSelectionBody: Pick a device from the list to see what it can do.

access.partialHint: This device holds only some of the capabilities this grant confers. Toggle it off and on to bring it back in line.

reason.mirrorOnly: From the local mirror — this host could not be asked.
reason.deviceRevoked: Revoked devices hold nothing, whatever the local record still says.
reason.lockedUseUnavailable: This grant has no enforcement point on this build, so it cannot be handed out.
reason.ownerMismatch: This device belongs to a different person than the one signed in here, so the host is not honouring its grants. Nothing was revoked — they take effect again for the person it belongs to.

access.revokedBody: It holds no capabilities and cannot reconnect without pairing again.

notApplicable.local: This machine does not grant itself access.
notApplicable.remote-host: A remote host decides what this client may do; grants are administered on the host, not here.
notApplicable.worker: A worker's capabilities come from its enrollment. Revoke it from Settings → Fleet to withdraw them.
notApplicable.ssh-host: An SSH host is reached with a key or a password, not with a grant. Access is decided by the server's own configuration.

access.title: Access
access.ownerSuspendedHint: Grants suspended: this device belongs to someone else.
access.terminalReachesSsh: This grant also lets the device open any SSH host saved on this machine. The host connects with the key or password it keeps, and the saved list is shared across granted devices rather than chosen per device.
access.sshFilesReachIsWhole: This grant has no folder limit. SFTP paths are that machine's own absolute paths and it resolves its own symlinks, so there is no root to confine this to.
access.revokeConfirmBody: Revoking is permanent. The device loses every grant and its key, and has to pair again to come back. To stop it for now, pause it instead.
access.pauseHint: Pausing blocks this device until you resume it.

lifecycleBlocked.no-host: This browser is not connected to a Host, so a pause, resume or revoke has nowhere to go.
lifecycleBlocked.needs-desktop-shell: Pausing, resuming and revoking need the desktop app on the Host.
lifecycleBlocked.not-owner: Only the Host's owner device may pause, resume or revoke a paired device.

runtime.probedVia: {count, plural, =0 {No worktrees} one {# worktree} other {# worktrees}} read over this host's own connection. Routing has not changed.

tierReason.osBackendUnavailable: The OS sandbox backend is not installed on this machine.
tierReason.containerAlwaysOnHostOnly: Runs only on an always-on host, in the project's runtime environment on its sandbox pool. Here a request for it is refused rather than run on this machine.
tierReason.microvmAdapterMissing: No microVM adapter is registered. Activate the E2B sandbox plugin; without it a microVM request is refused outright rather than falling back to the host.
tierReason.cuaDesktopNoConnection: Needs a bound machine that carries shell and file execution. A Docker connection provides it through `docker exec`, which runs inside the container. Cloud and Lume connections have no adapter yet, so they offer the remote desktop only.

reason.sandboxIsClientLocal: Sandbox connections are local to the machine running this window and are never routed to another device.
reason.sandboxNotHosted: This kind of device does not host sandboxes.
reason.sshShellOnly: SSH gives a shell and nothing else, so there is no workspace or sandbox to report.
reason.workspaceNotHosted: This kind of device does not host workspace environments.
reason.workerNoRoutingPlane: A worker receives dispatched work but is not on the device routing plane, so its workspaces cannot be read from here.
reason.routedToRemoteHost: This window currently routes execution to a remote host, so a workspace list would describe that host rather than this machine.
reason.activateToInspect: Activate this host to route execution to it and read its workspaces.

runtime.isRoutingTarget: Execution from this window currently routes here.
runtime.timingAuthorityHint: When set, only this machine arms scheduled work. Leave it off and every host arms its own; duplicates are absorbed by the deterministic idempotency key.

machines.total: {count, plural, =0 {No machines} one {# machine} other {# machines}}
machines.idleCost: A running machine keeps consuming CPU and memory until it is suspended or stopped, including across app restarts.
machines.shellWrongHost: A shell into a machine runs where the machine does. These belong to this computer, and the terminal is currently pointed somewhere else.
machines.shellFailed: Could not open a shell in the machine

shellState.paused: {name} is paused. Resume it below, and its memory comes back with it.
shellState.stopped: {name} is stopped. Start it below. Anything not on a bind mount is still there.
shellState.absent: Docker has no container for {name} any more. Start it below to create one.

activity.dispatchNotAddressable: This device is not addressed by the dispatch queue.
activity.dispatchEmptyBody: No work has been queued to this device.
activity.providesNothing: This device offers nothing a placement decision can match, so it will never be selected automatically.
activity.placementHint: Requirements are matched per dimension. A device that offers nothing in the dimension a caller asks for is reported as a capability mismatch rather than omitted.

host.renameFailed: Couldn't rename this host. Try again.
host.removeBody: {label} will be forgotten, along with its stored credential. Pair with it again to reconnect.

version.hostBehind: This host serves command contract v{host}, and this app was built for v{app}. Update the host to the same release as this app.
version.hostUnversioned: This host predates command contract versions, and this app was built for v{app}. Update the host to the same release as this app.
version.hostAhead: This host serves command contract v{host}, newer than this app (v{app}). Update this app to the same release as the host.
version.halfUpdated: This host's server ({server}) and brain ({brain}) come from different builds, so it cannot run work. Update the host so both come from one release.
version.updateRequested: The host will update as soon as nothing is running on it.
version.updateUnsupported: This host is from before self-update. Update it by hand once; after that it updates itself.
version.updateFailed: The host did not take the update: {error}

settingsLink.pairedBody: {count, plural, =0 {No devices are paired.} =1 {One device is paired.} other {# devices are paired.}} Grants, capabilities and lifecycle are managed in the device console.
settingsLink.hostsBody: {count, plural, =0 {No hosts are configured.} =1 {One host is configured.} other {# hosts are configured.}} Capabilities, workspaces and live presence are in the device console.

standaloneBody: Nothing is paired and this app is not running its own host, so there is no fleet to show and no host to ask about grants or lifecycle state. What is below describes this machine.

addHost.description: Pair with a machine running cognia-server so this app can drive its terminal, files, and git.
addHost.title: Add a remote host

wan.title: WAN connection
wan.description: Whether this desktop keeps a relay connection open so the device can reach it from anywhere.

reason.automatic: This device has been active recently, so a relay connection is kept open for it and it can be reached from any network.
reason.woken: A relay connection is being held open because you asked for one. It lasts until the device checks in or the app restarts, after which the usual rule applies again.
reason.dormant: This device has not checked in for over 30 days, so no relay connection is kept open for it. Each open connection costs a permanent socket, and they cannot be shared. The pairing, its keys and its permissions are untouched: connect it below, or the device reconnects by itself the next time it checks in.
reason.blocked: This device is paused or revoked, so the host refuses its requests and a relay connection could not serve one. Resume it under Access first.
reason.unprovisioned: This device was paired before relay connections existed, so it has no room to join. Pair it again to give it one.
reason.disabled: Relay connections are switched off for every device in Settings, so nothing is kept open and connecting here would not help.
reason.unmanaged: Only the desktop app keeps relay connections open. This shell cannot tell whether one is held for this device, or start one.

wan.liveHint: This says whether a connection is kept open, not whether the device is answering right now. Relay settings shows the live status of each one.

files.title: Files
files.unknownProfile: This row does not name a saved SSH host, so there is nothing to browse.
files.credentialRequired: Files on “{name}” open over the same login as its shell, and it uses a password that is not saved yet.
files.credentialRequiredBastion: Files on “{name}” are reached through “{bastion}”, which uses a password that is not saved yet.
files.chainBroken: “{name}” goes through a jump host that was removed, loops back, or is more than five hops deep, so its files cannot be reached.
